newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends shade up in range trade.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends shade up in range trade.

text.p: The Philippine peso finished a shade higher on Monday at 26.362 from 26.363 after some banks lightened their dollar holdings, traders said.

The peso moved in a narrow band from 26.359/26.362 in light trade as dollar inflows were held back by a belief the Central Bank could raise on Tuesday its overnight borrowing rate which at present is at 10 percent, dealers said.
This would be in line with the increase in Treasury bill rates at the regular auction on Monday.
"It's better to sell dollars now. If the Central Bank raises rates, arbitrage money will come in. It's better to buy the dollar when it's lower," a dealer said.
Traders said they saw the Central Bank stepping in to the market to buy about $16 million at 26.36 to limit the peso's strength after banks reduced their dollar holdings.
Volume was light at $119.5 million from $148.9 million.
